implementationPlan.description: Study the template before writing an arm, because the shape is load-bearing and the file already answers every question. Read tests/security/integrity-hostile-cases.ts:265-297 -- `codecCases` for PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_CODEC_LAYERS is the exact model: one `before`, one `after`, one `racing`, each naming the constant, each carrying an explicit `{code, layer}` expectation built with `layerOf(CONSTANT, "MEMBER")`, and each with a comment explaining WHY that layer is provably the branch that answered. Note the four helpers at :170-187: `before` (BEFORE arm), `after` (AFTER arm), `forged` (AFTER arm PLUS an `integrity` thunk), and `racing` (RACE arm, run through `probeRacing(RACE_BOUND, left, right)`). USE `forged`, NOT `after`, FOR THE DIGEST ARM: integrity-boundaries.security.ts has a separate assertion that re-seals at least one forgery per digest-bearing boundary by filtering `entry.arm !== "RACE" && entry.integrity !== undefined`, so a plain `after` would satisfy the three-arm count and still leave GRAPH_CONTENT uncovered by the reseal check. Finally note the assembly at :1204 -- `INTEGRITY_HOSTILE_CASES` spreads thirteen named arrays; you will add a fourteenth and must spread it there or the cases exist and are never collected.
implementationPlan.note:
Template re-read, plus the two projectors the reject turns on.

HELPERS (:174-190): `before`/`after` build a RefusalCase, `forged` = AFTER + an `integrity` thunk, `racing` routes both legs through `probeRacing(RACE_BOUND, left, right)`. `layerOf(CONSTANT, "MEMBER")` reads the layer OUT of the declared constant.

THE DECISIVE ASYMMETRY between the two projectors, which is the whole reject: `asLayered` (:197) returns non-objects unchanged and otherwise only RE-KEYS top-level fields — it never throws, so an ADMITTED sibling leg arrives as `{ok:true}` and `admitted()` at integrity-boundaries.security.ts:70-78 reddens it. `soleIssue` (mine) VALIDATES and threw. In `probeRacing` every leg is caught (`{status:"rejected", reason}`), `legValue` (:83) hands the Error to `admitted()`, an Error has no `ok`/`authority`/`truth`/`outcome`, so :204-205 and the whole-slice invariant at :214 both PASS on the admission. The 13 siblings never had this hole.

Also re-read the consumers a new arm touches: the three-armed ratchet (:122-132) only COUNTS arms; the reseal set (:135-153) is exact set equality over `arm !== "RACE" && integrity !== undefined`, so a plain `after` arm changes nothing there (GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS already earns its place via the `forged` arm); the collected-count invariant (:218) is computed from the case lists, so a new arm needs no hand-kept number.

Production layer for the missing code, read at packages/scheduler/src/graph-content.ts:222-226: `refuse("GRAPH_CONTENT_NONCANONICAL", "GRAPH_CONTENT_IDENTITY", ...)` — IDENTITY, not CODEC, and it sits AFTER the digest recompute (:216), which is why the two IDENTITY guards do not subsume each other.

implementationPlan.description: Write the three arms in tests/security/integrity-hostile-cases.ts as a new `graphContentCases` array, following `codecCases` in structure and comment discipline. The subject is landed and green: `encodeGraphContent` / `decodeGraphContent` from the bare `@moe/scheduler` root -- go through the published codec, never `canonicalGraphJson` or the raw hash, which are deliberately withheld so no consumer can mint bytes the kernel never accepted. `GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS` has three members (GRAPH_CONTENT_CODEC, GRAPH_CONTENT_IDENTITY, GRAPH_VALIDATION) and `GRAPH_CONTENT_ISSUE_CODES` offers DIGEST_MISMATCH, MALFORMED, NONCANONICAL, NOT_BYTES, TOO_LARGE, UNREADABLE and UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA. Suggested shape, and PREFER SPREADING THE THREE LAYER MEMBERS ACROSS THE THREE ARMS so the whole constant is exercised rather than one member three times: BEFORE -- bytes that never become content (truncated or not-bytes) refusing at GRAPH_CONTENT_CODEC, where nothing later on the path is reachable; FORGED/AFTER -- encode a valid content, then carry its digest onto a different content so shape and canonicalisation both pass and ONLY the re-derived digest comparison can refuse, at GRAPH_CONTENT_IDENTITY, with the `integrity` thunk re-sealing through production and asserted ok:true first; RACE -- a re-spelled canonical encoding raced against a non-canonical or duplicate-key variant. Assert the exact code AND layer on every arm, never merely that the call failed. Then spread `graphContentCases` into `INTEGRITY_HOSTILE_CASES` at :1204.

EDIT 1 — `soleIssue` no longer throws on an admission. Added `if (record["ok"] !== false) return value;` before the issue-count check, so `{ok:true,value}` reaches the harness UNCHANGED and `admitted()` reads its own `ok:true`. The throw is kept for a genuinely REFUSED result whose issue count is ambiguous (the case it was written for: picking issues[0] would pin whatever sortIssues ordered first). On a BEFORE/AFTER arm an admission now reddens twice — the whole-slice invariant collects it, then `assertRefusedWith` reports the absent code — instead of dying in a throw. Comment records the inversion mechanism so the next editor cannot re-introduce it.
